subject.title: feat(cron): configurable minimum interval guardrail for recurring jobs

question: Should OpenClaw core accept `cron.minInterval` as the operator-facing cadence guardrail for recurring cron jobs, with default-off behavior and enforcement when configured?
rationale: This adds a new core config/default surface that can reject or delay user-created recurring jobs, which is a product and compatibility contract rather than a purely mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Accept default-off core guardrail after cleanup
options.body: Proceed with this design once the generated docs map is refreshed, the branch is rebased, and exact-head checks pass.

options.title: Keep warning-only behavior
options.body: Reject enforcement in core and prefer a warning-oriented or documentation-only path for high-frequency cron schedules.

options.title: Move the policy out of core
options.body: Ask for a plugin or operator-specific policy surface instead of adding a new global core config key.

recommendation.title: Accept default-off core guardrail after cleanup
recommendation.body: Proceed with this design once the generated docs map is refreshed, the branch is rebased, and exact-head checks pass.
